The spec is unusually thorough, so my scan found only a handful of genuinely material gaps. Five questions queued; here's the first.

**Question:** If `extract` has already started writing files and then hits an unexpected error — the disk fills up, or the destination becomes unwritable partway through — must the tool undo the files it already wrote, or is it enough that it checked for all foreseeable problems before writing the first file? (FR-020)

**Why it matters:** This decides whether the tool needs a scratch-area-then-move design (more moving parts, but a truly all-or-nothing result) or can write straight into the destination. It also sets what "leaves no file behind at the destination" in SC-006 actually promises when a test simulates a full disk.

**Recommended:** Option B - Pre-flight validation catches every error the spec names (missing archive, bad format, conflicts, escaping paths), so writing directly into the destination is the smallest design that meets the spec. Guaranteeing rollback against I/O failures means staging every file elsewhere and moving it, which Constitution Principle IV (Simplicity) says to reject unless a stated requirement demands it — and best-effort cleanup is the worst of both, since a failure mid-cleanup leaves an undefined state while still looking like it tried.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Full atomicity: extract to a temporary staging area and move into place only after every member succeeds, so any failure leaves the destination byte-for-byte as it was |
| B | Pre-flight only: validate the whole archive (format, conflicts, unsafe paths) before writing anything; once writing begins, an unexpected I/O error exits non-zero with a diagnostic and leaves whatever was written in place, which the spec documents as a known limitation |
| C | Best-effort rollback: write directly, but on failure attempt to delete the files this run created |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (<=5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
